open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case file fixtures
open_points.text: Inputs: A contract version, input values by port, optional expected outputs, the actor. / for a file its digest, size and media type
open_points.question: For an authored trial case with file inputs or expected file outputs, does the operation receive the file bytes, merely file facts, or a separate upload/reference—and how can it persist the fixture if only facts are supplied?
options: File bytes are included in add_trial_case
Files are supplied through a separate prior operation and referenced
Only facts are supplied, with bytes obtained from another unspecified source
open_points.default_guess: Include bounded file bytes in add_trial_case and derive their facts in the kernel.

open_points.subject: flows.compose_flow_version constants
open_points.text: Inputs: A flow name, a purpose when new, ports, nodes, edges, guards, constants with declared classes, the actor. / A constant's StoredValue takes the value_schema and class the composing agent declared with it
open_points.question: Where does each constant's declared value_schema come from, since the operation's inputs mention only constants with declared classes?
options: Each constant explicitly carries a value_schema
The target port's schema is used
The schema is inferred from the literal
open_points.default_guess: Require each constant to carry an explicit value_schema.

open_points.subject: inspection of trial file fixtures
open_points.text: The owner receives every value. / a file — StoredValue fixture or SpooledFile — as digest, size and media type, its bytes only through read_spooled_file. / read_spooled_file takes only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue
open_points.question: Can the owner inspect the bytes of a trial-case file fixture, and if so through which operation?
options: Allow reading file-carriage StoredValues through a public read operation
Return fixture bytes in trial-case inspection
Fixture bytes are never readable, despite the owner-receives-every-value rule
open_points.default_guess: Extend the file-read operation to accept file-carriage StoredValues as well as SpooledFiles.

open_points.subject: agent view of approval previews
open_points.text: preview: what the owner saw — operation, target service, the built request and the input values; agents may read approvals, and an agent receives personal-data values only as digest and class / The request an approval covers is described ... by ... the full URL with its query ... [and] the JSON body's bytes
open_points.question: When personal-data inputs are embedded in the request URL, query, or JSON body, what exact request preview is returned to an agent without disclosing those values while still representing the approval?
options: Replace the whole request description with its digest and class
Redact individual personal-data-derived request components
Return the request description unchanged, which conflicts with K-14
open_points.default_guess: Return the request digest plus a structurally redacted description whose personal-data-derived components are digest-and-class only.

open_points.subject: inspection operation response fields
open_points.text: Records reach a caller as they are. / Return one contract version's ports and bounds. / Return one binding: status, effect class, key fields, declared classes, ports. / Return one flow version's graph.
open_points.question: Do get_contract_version, get_binding, get_flow_version, get_implementation and list_records return every field of their State 1 records, including identities, ownership and timestamps, or only the subsets listed by their module operations?
options: Return every model field, subject to masking
Return only each operation's explicitly listed subset
Use different completeness rules for get operations and list_records
open_points.default_guess: Return every model field for inspection, with code and personal-data masking applied separately.

open_points.subject: run answer lifecycle fields
open_points.text: A run's answer ... holds: run_id, the flow version, status, starter and times, outputs produced, waiting points ... and ... released_by and released_at / Candidate fields: ... cancelled_by ... resumptions ...
open_points.question: Does a run answer include cancelled_by and the resumptions history, and which timestamps are included by the phrase 'times'?
options: Include all M19 lifecycle fields
Include only started_at, ended_at and release fields, omitting resumptions and cancelled_by
Return different fields from get_run and list_records
open_points.default_guess: Include all M19 lifecycle fields in every run answer.

open_points.subject: spool ceiling during node execution
open_points.text: store.spool_file ... Errors: refused over a spool ceiling ... the caller concludes the element / effects.reach_operation_element ... any refusal or error of a module it calls that is not one of those is internal_error
open_points.question: When store.spool_file refuses a service output for exceeding a spool ceiling, must effects convert it to the specified contract_violation/applied conclusion, or treat the called-module refusal as internal_error?
options: Convert it to contract_violation with the EffectAttempt applied
Treat it as internal_error
Make spool_file return a non-refusal check result for ceiling excess
open_points.default_guess: Treat ceiling excess as an expected result and record contract_violation with the non-read attempt applied.

open_points.subject: record_change actor for automatic records
open_points.text: Every operation that writes a record receives the acting Actor M27 ... from its caller / record_admission_verdict ... writes AdmissionVerdict M08, and Activation M09 when admitted / activation by the kernel / activate_flow_version ... actor kernel for read, owner otherwise
open_points.question: For one store change initiated by an agent or owner but containing a kernel-authored automatic Activation or FlowActivation, is the change's single actor argument the requester, the kernel, or are actors supplied per written record?
options: Supply an actor per record in the change payload
The change actor is the requester, with automatic records overriding it internally
Split automatic records into a separate kernel-actor store change
open_points.default_guess: Supply each record's actor explicitly and use kernel for automatic activations.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes
open_points.text: Inputs: One JSON value. / Errors: refused for ... a duplicate key. / module:surface turns every JSON text a request carries ... into its canonical form with canonical_values.canonical_bytes
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text or an already parsed JSON value, and where are duplicate object keys detected before parsing discards them?
options: Accept raw JSON text and parse with duplicate-key detection
Accept a parsed value plus parser evidence that no duplicate occurred
Detect duplicates entirely in surface before calling canonical_bytes
open_points.default_guess: Accept raw JSON text at the surface boundary with duplicate-key detection, while internal callers use parsed values that are already valid.

open_points.subject: service_invoker.send_prepared_request failure_detail
open_points.text: Outputs: ... a bounded failure_detail. / The body of an error response is not interpreted; at most failure_detail_bytes_max of it is kept as failure_detail
open_points.question: For each transport and HTTP outcome, when is failure_detail present and what bytes or text does it contain, including malformed responses, connection errors, timeouts and non-UTF-8 error bodies?
options: Only error-response body excerpts produce failure_detail
Transport failures use a fixed closed diagnostic text and error bodies use a defined decoding rule
Implementations may emit any bounded sanitized diagnostic
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed diagnostics for transport failures and a deterministic UTF-8-safe excerpt rule for error bodies.

open_points.subject: successful runs with guarded outputs
open_points.text: succeeded when every node and output concluded successfully / run.succeeded <-> for_all node: conclusion IN {succeeded, skipped_by_guard} / A flow output that a guard can leave unproduced is allowed
open_points.question: Can a run be succeeded when a flow output is skipped_by_guard, or must every flow output be produced successfully?
options: Skipped-by-guard nodes and outputs permit a succeeded run
Any unproduced flow output makes the run failed
open_points.default_guess: Permit a succeeded run with skipped_by_guard outputs, following A13.

open_points.subject: orphan content-addressed files after partial operations
open_points.text: When a request makes several store changes, those made before the failed one stay / put_value_bytes ... The bytes exist in the content-addressed area / The only files the kernel keeps beyond a run are the file fixtures of trial cases
open_points.question: If bytes are published before the record-writing change fails, are unreferenced value or fixture files retained forever, removed immediately, or garbage-collected at startup?
options: Retain unreferenced bytes indefinitely
Delete bytes when the later record change fails
Remove unreferenced content-addressed files during startup recovery
open_points.default_guess: Remove newly published bytes when their owning record change fails, provided no existing record references them.

open_points.subject: surface behavior after ordinary internal_error
open_points.text: Any request answered internal_error therefore stops the kernel once the answer is sent / internal_error ... the caller re-reads before repeating / stop_required ... module:surface answers internal_error ... and ends the process
open_points.question: Does every ordinary internal_error terminate the kernel after the response, or only stop_required and startup failures?
options: Every answered internal_error terminates the process after responding
Only stop_required terminates the process
Store-related internal_error terminates, while other internal errors do not
open_points.default_guess: Terminate after every answered internal_error, as required by A14 rule 7.

open_points.subject: ignored spool-removal failure
open_points.text: A spool that cannot be removed then is removed at the next start / remove_run_spool ... Errors: internal_error on an I/O failure; its caller does not fail the request on it
open_points.question: When spool removal returns internal_error but the request still succeeds, does the kernel continue serving, stop after the successful response, or merely log the failure?
options: Continue serving and retry cleanup only at the next restart
Stop after returning the successful run result
Convert the request result to internal_error and stop
open_points.default_guess: Continue serving, record no new kernel fact, and retry cleanup at the next start.
